lessons.title: The closing sprint for a first crown
lessons.subtitle: A tied title race became a decisive winning run.

story.title: A race still open
story.body: With three fixtures left in 1966–67, Toluca and América were level on points. América drew twice while Toluca won each remaining match.

story.title: Dosal delivers
story.body: Juan Dosal scored twice against Necaxa in the clinching victory. Toluca had its first league crown after fourteen years in the top division.

facts.label: Rival in the closing title race
facts.prompt: Which club was level on points with Toluca with three matches remaining in the 1966–67 title race?
facts.scope: 1966–67 league title race; three matches remaining.
facts.evidence: The club identifies América as level with Toluca before the final three fixtures.

facts.label: Closing winning run
facts.prompt: How many consecutive victories closed Toluca’s first league-winning campaign in 1966–67?
facts.scope: Final three fixtures of the 1966–67 league campaign.
facts.evidence: Toluca’s account records three straight wins.

facts.label: Scorer in the title-clinching match
facts.prompt: Who scored twice for Toluca against Necaxa to seal the club’s first league title?
facts.scope: Toluca’s title-clinching match in the 1966–67 league campaign.
facts.evidence: The retrospective attributes both goals to Juan Dosal.

lessons.title: A third crown in a different format
lessons.subtitle: A points-based final group decided the championship.

story.title: Four clubs, one title
story.body: In 1974–75, Toluca entered a final group with Atlético Español, León and Curtidores. Each club faced its three rivals twice; the points leader would take the championship.

story.title: Estupiñán’s decisive finish
story.body: An Ítalo Estupiñán goal beat León at home. Toluca reached eight points and secured its third league title with a fixture still to play.

facts.label: Score that clinched the third title
facts.prompt: What was Toluca’s score against León in the home match that clinched its 1974–75 league title?
facts.scope: Title-clinching home match, 1974–75 final-stage group; not an aggregate.
facts.evidence: The club records a one-goal home win over León.

facts.label: Scorer of the decisive goal
facts.prompt: Who scored Toluca’s decisive goal against León in the 1974–75 title-clinching match?
facts.scope: Toluca’s 1974–75 title-clinching home match against León.
facts.evidence: The club names Ecuadorian forward Ítalo Estupiñán as the scorer.

facts.label: Points at clinching
facts.prompt: How many final-stage group points had Toluca accumulated when it clinched the 1974–75 title?
facts.scope: Points at the title-clinching moment, with one fixture still pending; not the final season total.
facts.evidence: The retrospective gives eight points and one match still to play.

lessons.title: A commanding start to the millennium
lessons.subtitle: Two final legs brought another title.

story.title: The league leader advances
story.body: Enrique Meza’s Toluca topped the Verano 2000 regular season. It eliminated Puebla and Guadalajara to reach another final.

story.title: A decisive two-leg finish
story.body: Toluca won away at Santos before completing the final at the Nemesio Díez. The aggregate secured the club’s sixth league title.

facts.label: Away final-leg score
facts.prompt: What was Toluca’s score away to Santos Laguna in the first leg of the Verano 2000 final?
facts.scope: Verano 2000 final, away first leg; Toluca shown first.
facts.evidence: The account gives a two-goal away victory.

facts.label: Final aggregate
facts.prompt: What was Toluca’s aggregate score against Santos Laguna across the Verano 2000 final?
facts.scope: Verano 2000 two-leg final aggregate; Toluca shown first.

facts.label: Coach of the championship team
facts.prompt: Who coached Toluca’s Verano 2000 league-winning team?
facts.evidence: The team is identified as coached by Enrique Meza.

lessons.title: Bringing the trophy home from Monterrey
lessons.subtitle: A level first leg left everything to play for away.

story.title: An open final
story.body: Toluca eliminated Cruz Azul and Pachuca in the Apertura 2005 playoffs. Monterrey then drew the first final leg at the Nemesio Díez.

story.title: Sánchez makes the difference
story.body: Vicente Sánchez stood out in the away-leg victory. Toluca secured its eighth league title and, in the club’s account, its first championship clinched away from home.

facts.label: Home final-leg score
facts.prompt: What was Toluca’s score at home to Monterrey in the first leg of the Apertura 2005 final?
facts.scope: Apertura 2005 final, home first leg; Toluca shown first.

facts.label: Away final-leg score
facts.prompt: What was Toluca’s score away to Monterrey in the second leg of the Apertura 2005 final?
facts.scope: Apertura 2005 final, away second leg; Toluca shown first.
facts.evidence: The club records a 3–0 victory in Monterrey.

facts.label: Standout player in the away leg
facts.prompt: Which Toluca player does the club’s account single out for his performance in the Apertura 2005 final away leg?
facts.scope: Official Toluca retrospective of the Apertura 2005 second leg; no individual goal total inferred.
facts.evidence: The club credits an outstanding Vicente Sánchez performance.
